verification_policy: Only read primary-source statements are marked checked. Dataset mirror integrity, owner-reported scores and inference are separate. No automated DrivenData refresh.

sources.title: GEMS problem, target, metric and GeoTIFF requirements
sources.claim: Target is geological faults. Expert-labelled new faults form the initial test set; the final set is expanded through expert review. DTI uses alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, triangular 300 m support. Single float32 band, EPSG:32611, 100 m, template bounds, [0,1], null/NaN outside.
sources.scope: Both chunks read; no later automated reads after Terms discovered. No hidden labels or band-order certification.

sources.title: GEMS Official Rules, September 2026, report 96647
sources.authority: DOE / National Laboratory of the Rockies
sources.claim: Three submissions per week; one final entry for both prize rounds; eligibility verification; complete reproducibility assets for finalists; generative-AI-use disclosure required in the narrative. Appendix A deadline is 5 p.m. ET on the deadline date.
sources.scope: All seven returned chunks read through the end of §A.17. Key date itself deferred to the competition website. This is not legal advice or an eligibility certification.

sources.title: DrivenData Terms of Use — Prohibited Uses
sources.claim: Prohibits robot/spider/automatic device or process access for any purpose, including monitoring or copying.
sources.scope: First two chunks read, including the specific prohibition. Initial requested agent source review preceded discovering this term; not a human-read snapshot. No recurring scraper or automated upload implemented.

sources.title: Public leaderboard snapshot
sources.claim: Initial tool retrieval showed DARD 0.3195, nchuzhoy 0.3128, alexoktaba 0.3042, and account wbg1 at 0.2477.
sources.scope: Snapshot, not permanent/live ranking. Rows do not identify submission filenames. H25/file-to-score mapping is owner-reported, not receipt-verified. No later automatic access.

sources.title: Organizer reference solution
sources.claim: Official reference repository provides a simple baseline and CPU/GPU environments; requires competition data placement.
sources.scope: Repository overview read, not independently reproduced here. Our implementation is separate.

sources.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners — He et al., CVPR 2022
sources.claim: Random input patches are masked and reconstructed; example masking 75%; original design uses an asymmetric visible-patch encoder and lightweight decoder.
sources.scope: This objective motivates our small convolutional masked autoencoder. Our architecture is not a ViT MAE replication, and the paper does not validate faults in Nevada.

sources.title: Foundation Models for Generalist Geospatial Artificial Intelligence — Jakubik et al., 2023
sources.claim: Prithvi pretrained on >1 TB HLS multispectral satellite imagery and fine-tuned on flood, burn-scar and other Earth-observation tasks; reduced-label experiments support data efficiency.
sources.scope: Not evidence that geophysical reconstruction errors identify faults. HLS spectral weights are not directly compatible with the 19 heterogeneous feature channels. No NASA weights used here.

sources.title: IBM Research and NASA IMPACT release Prithvi
sources.claim: NASA describes self-supervised foundation-model training, HLS imagery, the August 3, 2023 release, temporal ViT, flood mapping and burn-scar applications.
sources.scope: Official NASA confirmation of precedent only. A guessed shorter NASA URL returned 404 and was replaced, not used as evidence.

sources.title: GeoDAWN airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys
sources.claim: Surveys span 51,857 km², 149,030 line-km, four acquisition blocks; east–west flight-line spacings 200 m (Area 1) and 400 m (Area 2); variable clearance and magnetic processing corrections matter.
sources.scope: USGS ScienceBase item JSON reports a 2025-02-28 source update, the release spatial bounding box, and archived Area-1/Area-2 grid ZIP metadata. The item describes magnetic and radiometric products. Listed ZIPs: 22103_area1_grids.zip (44,487,393 bytes) and 22103_area2_grids.zip (238,439,415 bytes). Direct binary HEAD to ScienceBase closed at TLS in this sandbox; archive contents, radiometric channel names/units and exact competition-grid coverage are not verified. Release extent is not the same as cellwise coverage.
sources.license: USGS data release; retain original metadata and attribution

sources.title: INGENIOUS regional compilation, GDR 1391
sources.claim: Publicly accessible CC BY 4.0 regional datasets: faults, geodetics, gravity/magnetics, conductance, heat flow, thermal probes, wells/springs, volcanic and paleo-geothermal features.
sources.scope: Official catalog availability/license verified, not every underlying binary downloaded this run. Contributors explicitly disclaim fitness/errors.

sources.title: INGENIOUS thermal-conductivity source categorization, GDR 1390
sources.claim: TC in this resource means thermal conductivity; data categories distinguish known measured, assumed measured and unmeasured/estimated values. Publicly accessible CC BY 4.0.
sources.scope: Does NOT identify the meaning of the ambiguous tc BAND in our owner bridge. Do not equate its name with tilt angle, radiometric counts or this table without original band metadata.

sources.title: USGS 3DEP one-meter bare-earth DEM availability
sources.claim: A small in-region query returned seven matching tiles and two GeoTIFF URLs; an approximate broader regional query returned 1,454 matching metadata items with concrete GeoTIFF URLs and sizes. Metadata describes bare-earth lidar DEMs, public-domain distribution, NAVD88 elevations and possible seams across collection projects.
sources.scope: The broader bbox is approximate and does not certify full exact competition-footprint coverage. Direct binary HEAD to the listed S3 sample failed TLS in this sandbox; raw tile bytes, exact coverage, seam treatment and source datum mosaic are NOT verified. H27-CHANNEL-DEFLECT remains deferred.

sources.title: Blind geothermal system, Southern Gabbs Valley — Earney et al., GRC 2018
sources.authority: USGS / NBMG authors, DOE OSTI repository
sources.claim: Gravity, magnetics and MT constrain concealed basin structures; faults bound an intra-basin gravity high; conductive cap and magnetic low coincide with a thermal anomaly, with hydrothermal alteration an interpretation rather than a unique diagnosis.
sources.scope: Specific case study, not a validated classifier for the competition; lithologic boundaries also generate potential-field edges.

sources.title: Three-Dimensional Geothermal Fairway Mapping — Siler & Faulds
sources.claim: Heat and permeability must be collocated; fault intersections/tips, stress-favourable geometry and suitable lithology together determine fluid-flow fairways.
sources.scope: Fault prediction alone is not proof of a geothermal vent, resource or production well; this study uses independent 3D geological, well and seismic constraints not available to our model.

sources.title: Using Deep Learning to Map Quaternary Faults in Western USA — Hermant et al., SGW 2025
sources.claim: Fault scarps can create local topographic changes; catalogue homogeneity/accuracy vary; a mapped North Central Nevada example has local catalogue offsets up to 400 m. Faults can be fluid conduits or barriers.
sources.scope: The 400 m observation is not a measurement of this competition’s hidden truth or every catalogue trace. Institutional conference publication, not a government dataset.

sources.title: Census TIGER/Line roads (derived distance mirror)
sources.authority: US Census Bureau; mirror processing in GEMSDOE24
sources.claim: Official Census catalog provides annual TIGER/Line geographic shapefiles; the 2024 derived road-distance raster is pinned to the owner source-processing receipt.
sources.scope: This run restores/hash-checks the derived raster; it does not redownload county vector bytes or rederive road classes. Audit-only, never an encoder or fault-head input.

sources.title: BLM closed mining claims (derived distance mirror)
sources.authority: Bureau of Land Management; mirror processing in GEMSDOE24
sources.claim: Official service layer 2 is Closed Mining Claims, polygon geometry, NAD83 EPSG:4269; QLTY and disposition fields exist. The derived distance raster is pinned to an inherited source-processing receipt.
sources.scope: PLSS legal-land approximations, not exact workings/stakes. Not newly downloaded vectors in this run. Audit-only, no causal inference; no encoder/fault-head input.

sources.title: GEMSDOE24 exact H25-1 D1.5 file and code
sources.authority: Project owner, not an official scientific source
sources.claim: H25-1 is an exactly reproduced subset of H19-5: 121131→60069 pixels; 1.5px deterministic dot thinning. The owner reports 0.2477 versus parent 0.1922.
sources.scope: A platform receipt tying score to file is absent; H25’s old all-catalogue exclusion is leaky as a clean OOF baseline. Site still calls file unscored. See local forensics and holdout receipts.

sources.title: DOE-deposited INGENIOUS DOI metadata / public DataCite REST API
sources.claim: Registry identifies DOI 10.15121/1881483, INGENIOUS compilation, DOE Geothermal Data Repository publisher and metadata update 2025-03-07T03:05:37Z. DataCite documents public single-DOI GET retrieval.
sources.scope: Full returned registry response read; API request documentation first chunk checked. Registry updates are not GDR-file-change or binary-availability checks. API docs: https://support.datacite.org/docs/api-get-doi

sources.title: USGS ComCat FDSN Event Web Service
sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.claim: Official count query returned 14,502 ComCat records for M≥2.5, 1975-01-01 through 2024-12-31, in the GeoDAWN ScienceBase bounding rectangle.
sources.scope: Count/query availability only. It does not establish magnitude completeness, event location quality, fault association or alignment to the competition footprint. Full event records were not used in H27-SRCOH.

sources.title: Airborne radiometric data map alteration of porphyry copper systems in the Elkhorn district, MT
sources.authority: USGS publication record / Anderson et al., 2025
sources.claim: The USGS-hosted 2025 conference paper reports surficial K, Th and U maps, radioelement ratios and potassium-enhancement mapping that highlighted known and additional hydrothermal alteration in the Elkhorn district, Montana.
sources.scope: Geographic and deposit-type analogue only. It is not a Nevada fault detector, does not establish that GeoDAWN archive channels have those exact names/units, and does not validate the competition task.
